title: Global ODE and Log-density Integration Error

items.title: Finite geometric error bound from a one-step recurrence
items.statement: For h=T/N>0, p≥1, C,C₀,L≥0, and nonnegative errors satisfying e₀≤C₀h^p and eₙ₊₁≤(1+Lh)eₙ+Ch^(p+1), bound every eₙ by the finite geometric sum, including the L=0 branch.
items.strategy: Unroll the recurrence by induction, sum the geometric series when L>0, use (1+Lh)^n≤e^(Lnh), and handle L=0 directly.

references.title: Ernst Hairer and Gerhard Wanner, Introduction à l’Analyse Numérique, Chapter III: Équations Différentielles Ordinaires
references.locator: §III.3, PDF pp. 7–8 / printed pp. 63–64: propagation and accumulation of local error for one-step Runge–Kutta methods.

references.title: Tobias Embree, Lecture Notes on Numerical Analysis
references.locator: Lecture 34, §5.3, PDF pp. 190–192: the error recurrence, finite geometric sum, and fixed-interval global bound.

items.title: A continuous flow changes log density by minus its divergence
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a C¹ flow of diffeomorphisms Φₜ generated by x′=f(t,x), with positive initial density p₀ and common-time C¹ flow dependence, the transported density satisfies pₜ(Φₜ(x₀))=p₀(x₀)/det DΦₜ(x₀) and d/dt log pₜ(x(t))=−divₓf(t,x(t)).
items.strategy: Use the C¹ change-of-variables theorem to identify the pushforward density, use the variational equation for the flow Jacobian, then differentiate its positive determinant with Jacobi’s formula.

references.title: Ricky T. Q. Chen, Yulia Rubanova, Jesse Bettencourt, and David Duvenaud, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
references.locator: Theorem 1 and Appendix A, PDF pp. 3–4 and 13–14: instantaneous change of variables, flow Jacobian, and divergence trace.

references.title: George Papamakarios et al., Normalizing Flows for Probabilistic Modeling and Inference
references.locator: §4.1, PDF pp. 30–31, equations (75)–(81), and §4.2.1, PDF p. 32: continuous flow and its augmented log-density equation.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed only to invoke the library’s Lebesgue change-of-variables theorem when identifying the pushforward density; the Jacobian and ODE arguments use no choice.

items.title: Global error from uniform one-step defect and stability
items.statement: For an exact IVP solution on [0,T] and numerical states in a common compact tube, a one-step map with uniform local defect at most Ch^(p+1), stability factor at most 1+Lh, and initial error at most C₀h^p has max-grid error at most (C₀e^(LT)+C(e^(LT)−1)/L)h^p for L>0 and (C₀+CT)h^p for L=0.
items.strategy: Split each global error into propagated previous error and local defect, then apply the finite recurrence bound.

references.locator: §III.3, PDF pp. 7–9 / printed pp. 63–65: Theorem 3.1, local error, step-map Lipschitz stability, and global propagation.

items.title: Global divergence-integral error separates state and quadrature error
items.statement: Let q=−divₓf and ℓ(t)=ℓ₀+∫₀ᵗq(s,x(s))ds. If the numerical states have uniform error Kₓh^p, the scalar increment Qₕ has Lipschitz sensitivity at most hKq in its starting state, its exact-start quadrature defect is at most Dh^(q+1), and the initial scalar error is at most Cℓh^r, then max-grid scalar error is at most Cℓh^r+TKqKₓh^p+DT h^q.
items.strategy: Subtract exact and numerical scalar increments, split state sensitivity from quadrature defect, and sum the per-step bound over N=T/h steps.

items.title: Global continuous-flow log-density error from state and quadrature bounds
items.statement: Under Countable Choice and the hypotheses of the flow log-density identity and divergence-integral error theorem, the numerical scalar error in the continuous-flow log density is bounded by the separate initial, state-trajectory, and quadrature terms Cℓh^r+TKqKₓh^p+DT h^q.
items.strategy: Identify the exact divergence integral with log density using the flow identity, then apply the deterministic scalar error theorem.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited only through the exact density interpretation supplied by thm-continuous-flow-log-density-equation.

items.title: Euler global state and log-density error on a bounded C² tube
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, f is jointly C² on an open neighborhood of a compact convex tube, its exact flow maps are C¹ diffeomorphisms, and exact/numerical trajectories remain in that tube. Forward Euler for x′=f and ℓ′=−divₓf has local augmented defect Ch², one-step stability 1+Lh, and fixed-time global state and log-density error O(h), with explicit constants and a separate divergence-quadrature contribution.
items.strategy: Bound the derivative and Lipschitz constant of the augmented field (f,−div f), derive the Euler defect and stability from the tube bounds, then apply the state and separate-quadrature results.

title: Global ODE and Log-density Integration Error — Examples

items.title: Euler has state error but exact log-density quadrature for a linear flow
items.statement: Under Countable Choice, for x′=x on [0,1] with x(0)=1 and any positive continuous initial density, Euler produces xₙ=(1+1/N)ⁿ, so its terminal state error is e−(1+1/N)ᴺ, while the Euler divergence accumulator gives the exact terminal log-density change −1.
items.strategy: Solve the scalar flow exactly, compute the Euler state recursion, and sum the constant divergence contribution separately.

items.title: Zero state error can coexist with nonzero log-density quadrature error
items.statement: Under Countable Choice, for x′=tx on [0,1] with x(0)=0 and any positive continuous initial density, Euler has zero state error at every grid point but the left-Euler divergence update has terminal log-density error h/2; replacing only that update by midpoint quadrature makes the log-density exact.
items.strategy: Compute the exact flow derivative and divergence integral, then sum the left and midpoint quadrature rules while observing that the state remains identically zero.
